Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-1342", "title": "Childhood Vaccines", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Vaccines are injections (shots), liquids, pills, or nasal sprays that you take to teach the immune system to recognize and defend against harmful germs."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The germs could be viruses or bacteria ."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Some types of vaccines contain germs that cause disease."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "But the germs have been killed or weakened enough that they won't make your child sick."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some vaccines only contain a part of a germ."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Other types of vaccines include instructions for your cells to make a protein of the germ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "These different vaccine types all spark an immune response, which helps the body fight off the germs."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Your child's immune system will also remember the germ and attack it if that germ ever invades again."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "This protection against a certain disease is called immunity."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Babies are born with immune systems that can fight most germs, but there are some serious diseases they can't handle."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "That's why they need vaccines to strengthen their immune system."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "These diseases once killed or harmed many infants, children, and adults."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "But now with vaccines, your child can get immunity from these diseases without having to get sick."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "And for a few vaccines, getting vaccinated can actually give you a better immune response than getting the disease would."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Vaccinating your child also protects others."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Normally, germs can travel quickly through a community and make a lot of people sick."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "If enough people get sick, it can lead to an outbreak."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "But when enough people are vaccinated against a certain disease, it's harder for that disease to spread to others."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "The entire community is less likely to get the disease."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "This is called \"community immunity.\" Community immunity is especially important for the people who can't get certain vaccines."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "For example, they may not be able to get a vaccine because they have weakened immune systems."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Others may be allergic to certain vaccine ingredients."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "And newborn babies are too young to get some vaccines."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Community immunity can help to protect them all."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "They must go through extensive safety testing and evaluation before they are approved in the United States."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Some people worry that childhood vaccines could cause autism spectrum disorder (ASD)."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "But many scientific studies have looked at this and have found no link between vaccines and autism."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Can vaccines overload my child's immune system?"}, {"id": "S028", "text": "No, vaccines do not overload the immune system."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Every day, a healthy child's immune system successfully fights off thousands of germs."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "When your child gets vaccines, they are getting weakened or dead germs."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "So even if they get several vaccines in one day, they are being exposed to a tiny amount of germs compared to what they encounter every day in their environment."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Your child will get vaccines during well-child visits ."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "They will be given according to the vaccine schedule."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "This schedule lists which vaccines are recommended for children."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "It includes who should get the vaccines, how many doses they need, and at what age they should get them."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "In the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) publishes the vaccine schedule."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Following the vaccine schedule allows your child to get protection from the diseases at exactly the right time."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "It gives their body the chance to build up immunity before being exposed to these very serious diseases."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3063", "title": "Abscess", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "You can get an abscess almost anywhere in your body."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "When an area of your body becomes infected, your body's immune system tries to fight the infection."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "White blood cells go to the infected area, collect within the damaged tissue, and cause inflammation."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Pus is a mixture of living and dead white blood cells, germs, and dead tissue."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Bacteria, viruses, parasites and swallowed objects can all lead to abscesses."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Abscesses inside your body may not be obvious and can damage organs, including the brain, lungs and others."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Treatments include drainage and antibiotics."}]}, {"id": "MLP-313", "title": "Macular Degeneration", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Macular degeneration, or age-related macular degeneration (AMD), is a leading cause of vision loss in Americans 60 and older."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It is a disease that destroys your sharp, central vision."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You need central vision to see objects clearly and to do tasks such as reading and driving."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "AMD affects the macula, the part of the eye that allows you to see fine detail."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It does not hurt, but it causes cells in the macula to die."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Wet AMD happens when abnormal blood vessels grow under the macula."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "These new blood vessels often leak blood and fluid."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Blurred vision is a common early symptom."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Dry AMD happens when the light-sensitive cells in the macula slowly break down."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "A common early symptom is that straight lines appear crooked."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Regular comprehensive eye exams can detect macular degeneration before the disease causes vision loss."}]}, {"id": "MLP-295", "title": "Immune System and Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Your immune system is a complex network of cells, tissues, and organs."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Together they help the body fight infections and other diseases."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "When germs such as bacteria or viruses invade your body, they attack and multiply."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "The infection causes the disease that makes you sick."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Your immune system protects you from the disease by fighting off the germs."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "What are the parts of the immune system?"}, {"id": "S006", "text": "The immune system has many different parts, including: Your skin, which can help prevent germs from getting into the body Mucous membranes, which are the moist, inner linings of some organs and body cavities."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "They make mucus and other substances which can trap and fight germs."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "White blood cells, which fight germs Organs and tissues of the lymph system , such as the thymus, spleen , tonsils, lymph nodes, lymph vessels, and bone marrow ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "They produce, store, and carry white blood cells."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Your immune system defends your body against substances it sees as harmful or foreign."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "They may be germs such as bacteria and viruses."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "They could also be cells that are damaged from things like cancer or sunburn ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "When your immune system recognizes an antigen, it attacks it."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Part of this response is to make antibodies."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Antibodies are proteins that work to attack, weaken, and destroy antigens."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Your body also makes other cells to fight the antigen."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Afterwards, your immune system remembers the antigen."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "If it sees the antigen again, it can recognize it."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "It will quickly send out the right antibodies, so in most cases, you don't get sick."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "This protection against a certain disease is called immunity."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "There are three different types of immunity: Innate immunity is the protection that you are born with."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "It is your body's first line of defense."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "It includes barriers such as the skin and mucous membranes."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "They keep harmful substances from entering the body."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "It also includes some cells and chemicals which can attack foreign substances."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "Active immunity , also called adaptive immunity, develops when you are infected with or vaccinated against a foreign substance."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Active immunity is usually long-lasting."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "For many diseases, it can last your entire life."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "Passive immunity happens when you receive antibodies to a disease instead of making them through your own immune system."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "For example, newborn babies have antibodies from their mothers."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "People can also get passive immunity through blood products that contain antibodies."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "This kind of immunity gives you protection right away."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "But it only lasts a few weeks or months."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "What can go wrong with the immune system?"}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Sometimes a person may have an immune response even though there is no real threat."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "This can lead to problems such as allergies , asthma , and autoimmune diseases ."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "If you have an autoimmune disease, your immune system attacks healthy cells in your body by mistake."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Other immune system problems happen when your immune system does not work correctly."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "These problems include immunodeficiency diseases."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "If you have an immunodeficiency disease, you get sick more often."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Your infections may last longer and can be more serious and harder to treat."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "There are other diseases that can affect your immune system."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "For example, HIV is a virus that harms your immune system by destroying your white blood cells."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "If HIV is not treated, it can lead to AIDS (acquired immunodeficiency syndrome)."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "People with AIDS have badly damaged immune systems."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "They get an increasing number of severe illnesses."}]}, {"id": "MLP-1236", "title": "Tinnitus", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Tinnitus is often described as a ringing in the ears."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It also can sound like roaring, clicking, hissing, or buzzing."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "It may be soft or loud, high pitched or low pitched."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "You might hear it in either one or both ears."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "People with severe tinnitus may have trouble hearing, working or even sleeping."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Causes of tinnitus include: Hearing loss in older people Exposure to loud noises Ear and sinus infections Heart or blood vessel problems Meniere's disease Brain tumors Hormonal changes in women Thyroid problems Certain medicines Treatment depends on the cause."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Treatments may include hearing aids, sound-masking devices, medicines, and ways to learn how to cope with the noise."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "NIH: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders"}]}]
